latest_release.name: v3.0.0
latest_release.body:
ORAS Go v3.0.0 is the first stable release of the v3 line. It adds a configuration layer compatible with `containers/image`, a client builder, registry mirrors, policy and signature verification, content verification, and new push modes. It also reorganizes remote-registry configuration so that a registry owns the settings its repositories share.

**The module path has changed.** v3 is published as `github.com/oras-project/oras-go/v3`:

```diff
-oras.land/oras-go/v2
+github.com/oras-project/oras-go/v3
```

```sh
go get github.com/oras-project/oras-go/v3@v3.0.0
go mod tidy
```

The v2 and v3 module paths are distinct, so one application can import both while it migrates package by package. The minimum supported Go version is 1.26.

Start with the [Migration Guide](https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/blob/v3.0.0/MIGRATION_GUIDE.md). It has before-and-after code for every breaking change listed below.

## What's New

### Configuration and clients

* **Unified configuration**: `registry/remote/config.LoadConfigs` loads Docker credentials, containers `auth.json`, `registries.conf`, `policy.json`, `registries.d`, and certificate directories. The default path strategy follows `containers/image`. An experimental UAPI strategy is also available.
* **Configured clients**: `remote.ClientBuilder` builds clients, registries, and repositories with TLS, retries, credentials, token flow, warnings, logging, policy, and mirror settings applied consistently. Use `builder.NewRegistry(props)` and `builder.NewRepository(props)`.
* **Registry mirrors**: repositories created from registry properties try applicable mirrors for reads and fall back to the primary. Writes always go to the primary.
* **Policy and signatures**: `registry/remote/policy` enforces allow/deny policy, and a denial wraps `policy.ErrDenied`. `registry/remote/signature` verifies OpenPGP simple signatures with `registries.d` lookaside storage, resolving the lookaside location for each scope as it is used.
* **ORAS-specific `registries.conf` keys**: `[[registry]]` entries accept `token-flow`, `referrers-api`, and `blocked-realm-prefixes`, and mirrors inherit them from the primary.
* **Resource-scoped credentials**: the new `properties.Resource` names a registry, optionally narrowed to a namespace or repository. Credentials and token scope hints are keyed by it, so logins to two namespaces of one registry no longer overwrite each other. `credentials.StoreOptions.Hierarchical` adds longest-prefix namespace matching for containers `auth.json` (Podman/Buildah).
* **Bearer token flow**: `auth.Client.TokenFetcher` selects the token flow. The default tries the OAuth2 password grant and falls back to the distribution token flow when the realm rejects it with 400, 401, 404, or 405, so registries such as GitLab, GHCR, GCR, ACR, and Artifactory work without configuration. Set `CompositeTokenFetcher.StrictOAuth2` (or `token-flow = "oauth2"`) to disable the fallback.

### Content and transfer

* **Content verification**: `content.Verify`, `oras.Verify`, `oras.VerifyGraph`, and `oras.ExtendedVerify` check content integrity without writing it and collect per-node results in a report. `oci.Verify` sweeps an OCI image layout and reports missing, unreferenced, and leftover blobs, as well as invalid `oci-layout` or `index.json` files.
* **Unsafe push**: the `content.UnsafePusher` interface pushes content whose digest or size is not known up front, such as a stream or a tar built on the fly, and computes both while writing. It is implemented by `memory.Store`, `oci.Storage`, `oci.Store`, and `remote.Repository`, and is bounded by `MaxUnsafePushBytes` (4 GiB by default).
* **Push modes**: `MaxChunkSize` enables OCI chunked uploads and honors the registry's `OCI-Chunk-Min-Length`. `SingleRequestPushThreshold` pushes small blobs in a single `POST`. Both are opt-in, on `remote.Registry` and `remote.Repository`.
* **Fewer round trips on copy**: the opt-in `SkipExistsCheckBelowSize` skips the destination

# ORAS Go library

`oras-go` is a Go library for managing OCI artifacts, compliant with the [OCI Image Format Specification](https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec) and the [OCI Distribution Specification](https://github.com/opencontainers/distribution-spec). It provides unified APIs for pushing, pulling, and managing artifacts across OCI-compliant registries, local file systems, and in-memory stores. > [!Note] > The `main` and `v2` branches follow [Go's Security Policy](https://github.com/golang/go/security/policy) and support the two latest versions of Go (currently `1.26` and `1.27`). ## Getting Started ### Concepts Gain insights into the fundamental concepts: - [Modeling Artifacts](docs/Modeling-Artifacts.md) - [Targets and Content Stores](docs/Targets.md) ### Quickstart Follow the step-by-step tutorial to use `oras-go` v3: - [Quickstart: Managing OCI Artifacts with `oras-go` v3](docs/tutorial/quickstart.md) ### Examples Check out sample code for common use cases of `oras-go` v3: - [Artifact copying](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/oras-project/oras-go/v3#pkg-examples) - [Registry operations](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/oras-project/oras-go/v3/registry#pkg-examples) - [Repository operations](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/oras-project/oras-go/v3/registry/remote#pkg-examples) - [Authentication](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/oras-project/oras-go/v3/registry/remote/auth#pkg-examples) - [Credentials management](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/oras-project/oras-go/v3/registry/remote/credentials#pkg-examples) Find more API examples at [pkg.go.dev](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/oras-project/oras-go/v3). ## Versioning This project follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) (`MAJOR`.`MINOR`.`PATCH`), with `MAJOR` for breaking changes, `MINOR` for backward-compatible features, and `PATCH` for backward-compatible fixes. ## Branches - To migrate from `v2` to `v3`, see [MIGRATION_GUIDE.md](MIGRATION_GUIDE.md). - To migrate from `v1` to `v2`, see the [`v2` branch migration guide](https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/blob/v2/MIGRATION_GUIDE.md). ### main (v3 development) [![Build Status](https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg?event=push&branch=main)](https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/actions/workflows/build.yml?query=workflow%3Abuild+event%3Apush+branch%3Amain) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/oras-project/oras-go/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/oras-project/oras-go) The [`main`](https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/tree/main) branch is under active development for `v3` and may contain breaking changes. **Not recommended for production use.** ### v2 (stable) [![Build Status](https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg?event=push&branch=v2)](https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/actions/workflows/build.yml?query=workflow%3Abuild+event%3Apush+branch%3Av2) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/oras-project/oras-go/branch/v2/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/oras-project/oras-go) [![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/oras.land/oras-go/v2)](https://goreportcard.com/report/oras.land/oras-go/v2) [![Go Reference](https://pkg.go.dev/badge/oras.land/oras-go/v2.svg)](https://pkg.go.dev/oras.land/oras-go/v2) The [`v2`](https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/tree/v2) branch contains the latest stable release and is **recommended for production use**. New features and bug fixes from `main` will be backported to `v2` if applicable. ### v1 (end-of-life) [![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/oras.land/oras-go)](https://goreportcard.com/report/oras.land/oras-go) [![Go Reference](https://pkg.go.dev/badge/oras.land/oras-go.svg)](https://pkg.go.dev/oras.land/oras-go) The [`v1`](https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/tree/v1) branch has reached end-of-life and is no longer maintained. ## Community - Code of Conduct: [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - Security Policy: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) - Reviewing Guide: [Reviewing Guide](https://github.com/oras-project/community/blob/main/REVIEWING.md) - Slack: [`#oras`](https://cloud-native.slack.com/archives/CJ1KHJM5Z) channel on CNCF Slack
